chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Jamil ibn Darraj from Ismail al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"Five [types of wives] a man may divorce at any time: the pregnant one, the one into whom he has not entered [consummation], the one whose husband is absent, the one who has not yet menstruated, and the one who has despaired of menstruation."

key_terms.اَلَّتِي قَدْ يَئِسَتْ مِنَ اَلْمَحِيضِ: The one who has despaired of menstruation (menopausal)
key_terms.اَلَّتِي لَمْ تَحِضْ: The one who has not menstruated (pre-pubescent)
key_terms.اَلْغَائِبُ عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: The one whose husband is absent

ai.seo_question: Which five types of wives can a husband divorce at any time according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the five categories are distinguished by the absence of the 'period of waiting' (Iddah) constraint typically associated with menstruation, allowing for immediate divorce. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that divorce is most straightforward when the wife is not in a state of menstrual purity or pregnancy, which usually require specific waiting periods to ensure lineage clarity. The hadith underscores the flexibility in marital dissolution for these specific physiological states, reflecting the practical legal considerations of the time.
